PR Summary by Qodo

Add Save all for received files ✨ Enhancement 🧪 Tests 📝 Documentation 🕐 20-40 Minutes
AI Description

>
>• Add Save all to share received files in one batch or download them individually.
>• Skip files already saved and require another tap before downloading after a share-sheet failure.
>• Cover selection, failures, and byte-identical browser downloads with tests; document the behavior.
>
Merge Risk 🟡 Medium

Blast radius 🟡 Medium 💥 2 capabilities

- 2 affected capabilities within one bounded functional scope: received-media-saving. - The changed path starts at the Save all control, reads the page's received print/file/incoming state, and ends at the same user's share sheet or downloads. - These are one bounded received-media saving integration rather than separate capabilities for the helper, page, or browser APIs. - This is a distinct user operation within the same bounded received-media saving integration: an individual print tap hands one selected received file to the browser and updates the same deduplication state consumed by Save all. - It does not create an independent functional scope.
Behavioral complexity 🟡 Medium 🧩 Interacting branches, Coordinated invariants

- Before this PR there was no Save all state machine. - After the change, the implementation combines eligibility filtering with three interacting states: busy serialization, downloadNext fallback after a non-cancellation share failure, and handed deduplication across later taps. - The new correctness conditions are that only fully received non-own files are selected, a cancellation does not consume items, a failed download remains retryable, and no concurrent tap starts a second batch. - The share/download APIs are existing browser mechanisms; the complexity comes from their new interaction with retry and deduplication state.
Potential damage 🟡 Medium 🩹 Recoverable

- If the changed capability regresses, the user may be unable to hand off some or all eligible received files in that tap. - The files remain in the page's in-memory files map, and the handed set is only advanced after share success or a download attempt, so a later tap can retry under the implemented paths. - Recovery requires the page to remain open and the user to tap again; a reload or page loss removes the in-memory opportunity. - No persistent application state or external transaction is changed. - Generally recoverable by retrying Save all while the page and received File objects remain available. - A browser-level share/download failure may require switching from share to download on a later tap; automatic background repair is not present.
Assessed commit 3f2842b
Diagram

```mermaid graph TD UI["Save all tap"] --> Batch["Eligible files"] --> Choice{"Batch share available?"} -->|Yes| Share["Share sheet"] -->|Success| Handed["Handed IDs"] --> Toast["Status toast"] Choice -->|No| Downloads["Paced downloads"] --> Handed Batch -->|None| Toast Share -.->|Failure: next tap| Downloads ```
High-Level Assessment

>Keep the native batch share with paced-download fallback: sharing files one by one would require repeated user interaction, while packaging them would change what recipients receive. Keeping selection and handoff policy separate from the page also makes the failure paths testable. This is marked as a test PR and should not be merged.

🐞 Bugs (4) 📎 Requirement gaps (1)
1. Save all stays in download mode after one share failure 📎 Requirement gap
>
>Description >
> >
>tap() sets downloadNext to true after a non-cancellation share failure, but createSaveAll
>never clears it after the fallback download batch. Because the flag prevents the share check, every
>later tap—including taps after new photos arrive—downloads instead of trying the share sheet, and
>the existing test does not reach a later tap.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[web/saveall.js[R38-44]](https://github.com/jtbinith/qodo-hack-2026/pull/141/files#diff-1197fbbadbb14a53258dbd75d68b20c8bf37f2e49062120e60b6b11916a8861fR38-R44) > >```diff >+ if (!downloadNext) { try { sharing = !!canShare(list); } catch { sharing = false; } } >+ busy = true; >+ try { >+ if (sharing) { >+ try { await share(list); } catch (e) { >+ if (e?.name === 'AbortError') return; // cancelled: nothing happens, the photos stay available >+ downloadNext = true; >``` >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >In `web/saveall.js`, a failed share sets `downloadNext` permanently, although fallback downloading should last for only one batch. Later taps, including those after new files arrive, should be eligible to try sharing again. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- web/saveall.js[26-26] >- web/saveall.js[36-55] > >## Recommended Fix >In `tap()`, consume and clear `downloadNext` when starting the fallback download batch. For example, capture it with `const useDownload = downloadNext; downloadNext = false;` before the download decision, and use `useDownload` at the share decision so a subsequent tap can check `canShare` again. Add a test in `tests/saveall.test.mjs` that performs a third tap after the fallback batch and asserts that `share` is called again. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

>
>Description >
> >
>tap() downloads from a fixed ready snapshot without checking whether save(p) handed over an
>item during a download gap. On a laptop, tapping an individual photo that is later in an active Save
>all batch starts its download immediately, then the batch downloads it again.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[web/saveall.js[R52-53]](https://github.com/jtbinith/qodo-hack-2026/pull/141/files#diff-1197fbbadbb14a53258dbd75d68b20c8bf37f2e49062120e60b6b11916a8861fR52-R53) > >```diff >+ if (i) await wait(DOWNLOAD_GAP); >+ try { download(ready[i].file); handed.add(ready[i].pid); } catch (e) { console.warn('download failed', ready[i].file?.name, e); } >``` >
>
>Agent prompt >

Recheck a photo's handed-over or in-flight status immediately before each batch download; reserve a photo during an individual share and release that reservation if the share fails or is cancelled. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

3. Failed downloads receive no user warning 🐞 Bug
>
>Description >
> >
>tap() announces Downloading ${ready.length} before attempting the files, then catches a failed
>download() call only to log it. If starting one or more downloads throws, the person receives no
>notice that the announced batch was incomplete and must tap again to retry those files.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[web/saveall.js[R50-53]](https://github.com/jtbinith/qodo-hack-2026/pull/141/files#diff-1197fbbadbb14a53258dbd75d68b20c8bf37f2e49062120e60b6b11916a8861fR50-R53) > >```diff >+ toast(`Downloading ${ready.length}${more(arriving)}`); >+ for (let i = 0; i < ready.length; i++) { >+ if (i) await wait(DOWNLOAD_GAP); >+ try { download(ready[i].file); handed.add(ready[i].pid); } catch (e) { console.warn('download failed', ready[i].file?.name, e); } >``` >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A download can fail to start without any user-facing indication, despite the batch notification. >## Fix Focus Areas >- web/saveall.js[50-55] >## Recommended Fix >Count download-start failures, leave those photos eligible for retry, and show a user-facing failure or partial-batch message after the loop while preserving the truthful 'Downloading' wording for attempted downloads. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

4. An unresolved share blocks every later tap 🐞 Bug
>
>Description >
> >
>tap() sets busy before awaiting share(list) and only clears it when that await settles and
>reaches finally. If the browser's share promise never settles, later Save all taps return `Still
>saving` indefinitely, with no recovery or explanation of the stalled operation.
>
>
>
>Code >

>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A share promise that never settles leaves Save all permanently busy. >## Fix Focus Areas >- web/saveall.js[32-55] >## Recommended Fix >Add a bounded stalled-operation recovery path with a user-facing message and explicit retry. Guard state changes from late share settlements so a stale completion cannot mark a later batch handed over; avoid starting a second share while the original sheet is still active. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

5. Photos being verified vanish from the count 🐞 Bug
>
>Description >
> >
>saveBatch() counts arriving photos only in incoming, but the receive handler removes a completed
>transfer from that map before done() finishes its asynchronous hash verification and inserts it
>into files. A tap during that interval finds the photo in neither collection and can say `Nothing
>new to save` without mentioning that it is still being processed.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[web/saveall.js[17]](https://github.com/jtbinith/qodo-hack-2026/pull/141/files#diff-1197fbbadbb14a53258dbd75d68b20c8bf37f2e49062120e60b6b11916a8861fR17-R17) > >```diff >+ for (const fid of incoming.keys()) if (!fid.startsWith('thumb:') && !files.has(fid)) arriving++; >``` >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A completed transfer temporarily disappears from both the ready and arriving counts while its bytes are being verified. >## Fix Focus Areas >- web/index.html[208-235] >- web/saveall.js[10-18] >## Recommended Fix >Keep full-photo transfers represented as pending until verification finishes, or maintain a separate verification-in-progress set included in the arriving count.
